newsitem.title: CHINA: HK gold ends lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends lower in quiet trade.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold closed at US$323.00/323.50 per ounce on Tuesday, down from its open at US$323.40/323.90 an ounce.
Local tael gold ended at HK$2,991, down from its open at HK$2,998 a tael, traders said.
"The market opened on a strong note but it turned quiet in the afternoon. There is no special reason, it's just following the United States," a trader with a local firm said.
Others said the rest of the week would likely be a yawn, although some were keeping an eye on crude oil prices.
"Some of us are keeping an eye on oil sales from Iraq. If oil prices come off substantially, gold could follow," said another trader.
The United Nations on Monday approved Iraq's distribution plan for food, medicine and other supplies, which would help pave the way for a resumption of Iraqi crude oil exports.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society was -6.00 from the previous fix at -5.00.
